verified.entry_point: A real Gogs server process built from /app is driven over HTTP; mail is captured by a local SMTP sink. At the pinned commit a reset mail mints a code with ACTIVATE_CODE_LIVES and the completion route accepts it after RESET_CODE_LIVES has passed; an account-activation code resets a password; the validity probe reports an activation code as valid. All three were reproduced through the real routes before the tests were written.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security tests accept only a 4xx refusal with no side effect, so a panic or 500 on the same path fails the same assertion; the functional suite additionally keeps the legitimate completion working.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the code itself names the account it belongs to (the signed payload and tail identify one user); there is no neighbouring resource or proxy object to authorise instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the protected operation is a single unauthenticated code exchange, not a role or direction axis; the analogous per-route axis is catalogued as unlisted_route (miss-legacy.patch).
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the protected sink is a state-changing password completion; the only read-only route is the validity probe, which has its own security test and is fixed by the same verifier (miss-probe.patch covers the inverse mistake).
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalisation or adjustment step runs on the submitted code before verification; the code is used byte-for-byte.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the code is authenticated by a SHA-1 over server-held account data, so a malformed or modified code is already refused on the vulnerable tree; such a test would pass there and prove nothing.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, role or secret lookup can fail open on this path; the only input is the mailed code.
